state.success: The command ORs only STATUS2_TORMENT into the target's status2; it has no timer, DisableStruct field, attacker write, battle-type branch, controller command, or Random() call.
state.duplicate: An already-tormented target takes the encoded failure pointer with no command-local state mutation or Random() call. It leaves the existing bit set.

effectScript.ppAndRng: Both success and duplicate first execute ppreduce, then accuracycheck. Cmd_settorment itself owns zero Random() calls; the source accuracycheck executes its own Random() % 100 + 1 before the setter (unless an earlier AccuracyCalcHelper/protect return applies). Thus a duplicate can spend PP and take the preceding accuracy roll, but the setter supplies neither a timer draw nor any other local RNG draw.

admission.manualSelection: TrySetCantSelectMoveBattleScript rejects an ordinary selected move exactly when it equals gLastMoves[active], is not MOVE_STRUGGLE, and active status2 carries STATUS2_TORMENT. It cancels multi-turn moves; ordinary battles choose BattleScript_SelectingTormentedMove, while Palace uses its distinct selection script and palaceUnableToUseMove flag.
admission.limitations: CheckMoveLimitations marks every slot whose move id equals gLastMoves[battler] when MOVE_LIMITATION_TORMENTED is requested and status2 carries the bit. Duplicate slot ids are all marked, not just the last selected index. Its Encore and Choice-Band tests are independent later predicates in the same slot loop; their masks combine, and Torment itself neither reads nor clears either field.
admission.struggle: AreAllMovesUnusable runs the all-limitations mask; when all four slots are blocked it sets noValidMoves and the selection script. Move selection then replaces the chosen move with MOVE_STRUGGLE, clears noValidMoves, sets HITMARKER_NO_PPDEDUCT, and targets Struggle. The explicit manual-selection check excludes MOVE_STRUGGLE.

lifetime.battleInit: BeginBattleIntro calls BattleStartClearSetData, then BattleIntroGetMonsData copies each BattlePokemon and explicitly sets status2 = 0 for each non-Safari active battler before first action. BattleStartClearSetData also resets gLastMoves to MOVE_NONE.
lifetime.endTurn: No Torment timer or Torment-specific end-turn clear exists. The normal turn handoff clears STATUS2_FLINCHED only, so Torment persists across end turns until active-battler replacement or battle teardown/reinitialization.
lifetime.switch: Ordinary SwitchInClearSetData assigns active status2 = 0 and gLastMoves = MOVE_NONE.
lifetime.batonPass: Baton Pass masks status2 down to CONFUSION, FOCUS_ENERGY, SUBSTITUTE, ESCAPE_PREVENTION, and CURSED; STATUS2_TORMENT is absent and is therefore cleared. It then resets gLastMoves to MOVE_NONE.
lifetime.faint: FaintClearSetData assigns active status2 = 0 and gLastMoves = MOVE_NONE.

boundedRemainder: The OFF manifest exposes status2, active HP/PP/current move/RNG, controller state, party checksums, and framebuffer hashes, but not gBattlescriptCurrInstr, decoded message/result flags, gBattlerTarget, gLastMoves, selection-script pointers, noValidMoves, HITMARKER_NO_PPDEDUCT, or Choice/Encore fields. The trace proves the public target-owned bit, both Torment PP reductions, the all-identical-slot Struggle result without Tackle PP loss, persistence through two decision boundaries, and reproducible hashes. Exact branch PC/message, last-move ownership, Choice/Encore composition, and init/switch/faint/Baton-Pass lifecycle are source-pinned; no unsupported claim is made about a live switch, faint, Baton Pass, Palace, or manual attempt by the tormented battler. This is evidence only and adds no production registration.
